We Know How Sunrise on the Reaping Ends. That Doesn’t Change Its Impact.

📅 20 Mar 2025 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1839 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elle

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor.
  • Spoilers below for The Hunger Games books, including Sunrise on the Reaping.
  • In a recent development, re-reading the original The Hunger Games series in preparation for this review, I started experiencing nightmares.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

Spoilers below for The Hunger Games books, including Sunrise on the Reaping.

In a recent development, re-reading the original The Hunger Games series in preparation for this review, I started experiencing nightmares. Despite my generally overactive imagination, I would not call this normal. I read a lot of fiction, much of it politically prescient if not outright dystopian; if everything I consumed brought on such sleep paralysis demons, I’d call a doctor. But I shouldn’t be surprised that, now, Suzanne Collins’s young-adult trilogy began seeping into my subconscious, 15 years after I’d first turned its final page—especially considering that it’s now the latest in her series to become a feature film.

It has been revealed that the lead protagonist in Collins’s trilogy, Katniss Everdeen, spends the entire series battling such nightmares as the death toll escalates around her. After volunteering as a tribute in the Capitol’s annual Hunger Games, pitting children against each other in a fight to the death, her already difficult life in District 12 becomes outright dangerous. She inadvertently sparks a rebellion. She leads that rebellion. She loses countless loved ones. Those of us who read and adored the series know how it ends, but even those unfamiliar with Katniss’s struggle can take an educated guess. Protest rarely goes unpunished.

I can’t claim to have experienced anywhere near the trauma Katniss undergoes throughout Collins’s trilogy, but I have aged considerably since I first read those books, and what struck me most as I re-encountered familiar passages was how present they still felt. I’d expected some nostalgia whilst leafing through The Hunger Games, Catching Fire, and Mockingjay, and the same when I’d pick up Collins’s latest installment in the franchise, the prequel novel Sunrise on the Reaping. I had not expected to feel so disturbed. Or so furious.

This is the crowning achievement of Sunrise on the Reaping, which succeeds in the near-impossible task of making an well-trodden story feel as intimate and visceral as its predecessors. Reaping is the fifth Hunger Games novel and the second prequel installment after The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes, which chronicled the youth and radicalization of the future president of Panem, Coriolanus Snow. (Like the original trilogy, Songbirds was adapted into a hugely popular Lionsgate film in 2023, and Reaping’s own adaptation landed in 2026.) Reaping surges forward a handful of years, set nearly a quarter of a century before Katniss’s own Hunger Games.

According to recent reports, the story centers on Haymitch Abernathy, a beloved figure in The Hunger Games trilogy, in which he plays the role of the embittered if endearing drunk whose previous Hunger Games victory sets him up as mentor to Katniss and her District 12 partner, Peeta, for their own. In Reaping, Katniss and Peeta have yet to be born, but a young Haymitch knows their parents well. Here, Collins does a remarkable job of delivering what fans would call devastating “lore drops,” but she does so, for the most part, without resorting to cheesy or unnecessary Easter eggs. These minor characters—including Katniss’s parents, Burdock Everdeen and Asterid March—serve a clear purpose: to ground Haymitch in a familiar-but-reoriented District 12, where rebellion is yearned for but rarely acted upon.

Sources indicate that one of the few characters willing to risk their wellbeing in pursuit of justice is Lenore Dove, Haymitch’s girlfriend and a descendant of the Covey, a group of former nomads whom readers will recognize from Songbirds. Her conviction, her music, and her love (“like all-fire,” she claims, one of several Covey expressions employed throughout the book) steers Haymitch to her aid at the annual reaping ceremony, during which child tributes are selected for the Hunger Games. This year is a Quarter Quell, and the Capitol will demand twice as many boy and girl tributes as in an average year. After an unexpected execution takes place in the District 12 square, Haymitch finds himself rounded up with three other tributes and sent to spar for his life in the Gamemakers’ brutal arena.

This is, of course, not a spoiler: Haymitch wins. Collins first described Haymitch’s victory way back in 2009 with the release of Catching Fire, during which Katniss and Peeta watch a recap video of Haymitch’s Quarter Quell. Through Katniss’s eyes, the young Haymitch comes off as “snarky. Arrogant. Indifferent.” But what Katniss doesn’t know is that the footage she’s watching has been heavily edited to reorder the timeline of events in the arena, and to remove Haymitch’s repeated efforts to undermine the Capitol. When he wins the games, he does so not as a ruthless survivor, but as a rebel attempting to break the arena itself. And when he returns home as a reluctant victor, he pays for his revolution a hundredfold.

According to recent reports, we already knew from Catching Fire that, mere weeks after the Quell, President Snow orders Haymitch’s mother, brother, and girlfriend to be killed. But it’s something else entirely to experience those deaths on the page. In Sunrise on the Reaping, this mother, brother, and girlfriend are no longer nameless extensions of Haymitch himself; they are characters we’ve come to know (named Willamae, Sid, and Lenore Dove), whose deaths we dread despite their inevitability. Our anticipation does not ultimately erase our pain, just as pre-grieving an ailing loved one does not ultimately erase their loss. Collins understands this well, and she uses our emotions to target our instincts for both ignorance and apathy.

In the end, Haymitch’s own assumed apathy cannot hold. He drives away his friends and few remaining neighbors, turning to “sleep syrup” and rotgut liquor as he’s tormented by violent memories and recurring echoes of “The Raven” by Edgar Allen Poe, which, in the world of Panem, has been passed down through the generations to become Lenore Dove’s “name poem.” In Poe’s famous 1845 poem, an unnamed narrator mourns the death of his lover, his “lost Lenore.” He is caught between two dueling desires: the temptation to forget Lenore and the desperation to remember her. His late-night visitor, a raven who only repeats the word “nevermore,” insists upon remembrance, driving the narrator to conclude that only madness awaits him.

Haymitch makes a similar conclusion—for the time being, anyway—as he wakes half-drunk from nightmares but stays alive, Lenore Dove’s final wish having “condemned [Haymitch] to life.” (She begs that he not let another sun rise on a reaping day, thus giving the book its title.) And though the word-for-word replication of “The Raven” in Sunrise on the Reaping is one of Collins’s few missteps—later eliminated by the movie adaptation—drawing the reader away from Haymitch’s world, the poem nevertheless carries a deeply poignant message.

Thematically, much of Sunrise on the Reaping is about propaganda, and specifically how truth is manipulated to trigger an audience’s emotional response. The Capitol Gamemakers edit footage of Haymitch to confirm what Capitol residents already want to believe about him—that he is a charming but ultimately dangerous rascal—and to ignore what does not suit their “logic.” As Plutarch Heavensbee (another character from the original trilogy) tells Haymitch and his allies, “People have an emotional response to something, then they come up with an argument for why it logically makes sense.” That explains the so-called “necessity” of the Hunger Games themselves: By convincing the Capitol residents to fear and deride the Districts, and the Districts to fear and covet the Capitol, the Capitol citizens are able to stomach the Hunger Games as “for the greater good”—and the Districts ultimately succumb to the resulting authoritarianism. History, as they say, is written by the victors.

In a recent development, but while propaganda is indeed a form of storytelling, there is a chasm of difference between twisting stories with malicious intent and preserving them for posterity. Collins’s use of “The Raven,” in addition to numerous other songs and poems popular amongst the Covey, is a testament to that fact. That a poem from 1845 would exist, in its entirety, numerous centuries in the future—having survived the collapse of North American society and the building of a totalitarian government bent on killing children—is something of a wondrous idea to behold. It is also a nod to the strength and resilience of the Covey themselves, who have taken care to maintain these stories despite the Capitol’s relentless and well-documented censorship.

Industry observers note that as in Mockingjay and Songbirds, Sunrise on the Reaping ends with an epilogue. This final chapter leaps decades into the future, taking place in the years after Mockingjay and its siege on the Capitol. When Katniss and Peeta choose to compile a post-war “memorial book,” Collins writes that Haymitch is not initially interested in contributing. “What use?” she writes, from his perspective. “What point? To relive all the loss. But when Burdock’s page came up, I had to mention him showing me [Lenore’s] grave. And I felt compelled to tell them about Maysilee Donner, former owner of the mockingjay pin. And how Sid loved the stars. Before I knew it, they all came tumbling out: family, tributes, friends, comrades in arms, everybody, even my love. I finally told our story.”.

In a recent development, haymitch realizes that forgetting was never really an option. It wasn’t an option for the narrator of “The Raven,” nor is it an option for him. Choosing to forget would be capitulating to a system that manipulates such forgetfulness for power-hungry aims. Intentional amnesia, learned apathy—both would be an abdication of love.

Sources indicate that 15 years after Mockingjay was released, I needn’t wonder why the series brought on refreshed nightmares. Authoritarianism is not a fictional threat. It has not been dreamed up for our entertainment or titillation. It is here and present and bloodthirsty. As with the entirety of The Hunger Games saga, Sunrise on the Reaping keeps this truth close to its heart, which is why—even for a book for “young readers”—its story is so difficult to absorb.

Recent findings suggest that yet Collins makes it clear that the war against injustice did not start or end with Katniss Everdeen. Before her was Haymitch Abernathy. Before him was Lucy Gray Baird, of The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes. She learned her political anthems from the Covey, who learned them from their ancestors of yore. Stories, passed down through generations—each of them sowed the seeds of revolution that are sparked during Haymitch’s Hunger Games and ignited during Katniss’s. Dystopian literature like Sunrise on the Reaping is not a manual for effective protest, nor a crystal ball predicting the future. It is fiction and should be treated as such. But it can serve an essential purpose, one that Collins has not lost sight of in her decades of Hunger Games books: Fiction keeps close what we might otherwise deign to forget. It reminds us of what we stand to lose. And, at its best, it stirs us to pick up the fight.

This Piping Hot Zenith Collaboration Explains the Future of the Watch Market

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, in early July, I met with Zenith’s chief product officer Romain Marietta over Zoom to get a sneak peek at a watch that wouldn’t come out until November.
  • Zenith recently confirmed that it’s laying off roughly half of its current workforce as it attempts to shift its position in the market.
  • Lorel Monroy, a sales associate at LA’s Feldmar Watch Organization, tells me there’s “definitely been an uptick” in interest around Zenith this year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, in early July, I met with Zenith’s chief product officer Romain Marietta over Zoom to get a sneak peek at a watch that wouldn’t come out until November. The latest Zenith G.F.J., made in partnership with the Los Angeles-based independent watchmaker J.N. Shapiro, is a gorgeous timepiece that combines the former’s mechanical know-how with Shapiro’s meticulously handmade dials. Over four months before the watch was even unveiled to the public, Marietta shared that 20 of the 25 pieces produced had already been sold. Of all the releases from the major Swiss brands in 2026, none better represent the future of luxury watchmaking than this high-end, fussily made, independent-adjacent, sold-out-before-you-ever-heard-about-it G.F.J.

Zenith recently confirmed that it’s laying off roughly half of its current workforce as it attempts to shift its position in the market. “All of us in our segment, which is described as mid-range, are going through a very difficult period,” Zenith CEO Benoit De Clerck told staff as he explained the restructuring, according to Le Temps. The brand has been shifting upmarket since last year, when it released a rainbow gem-set version of its flagship sport watch. The G.F.J. is the cornerstone of that newly introduced business. As the economy tilts even further in favor of the uber-rich, it’s also altering where the bulk of the profits come from for watchmakers. “Wealthy people are still wealthy, and even more wealthy,” Marietta stated. “It’s easier [now] to sell high-end watches than watches for 3,000 to 5,000 Swiss francs.”.

Sources indicate that that’s true. Lorel Monroy, a sales associate at LA’s Feldmar Watch Organization, tells me there’s “definitely been an uptick” in interest around Zenith this year. Not for the brand’s flagship Chronomaster, which remains firmly in the starter luxury watch zone at $12,300, but for the far more expensive G.F.J., which starts at $49,900. “The luxury direction is the game changer,” Monroy said. Feldmar only received three G.F.J.s to allocate in 2026 and they were all promptly snapped up. There’s now a waitlist building at the retailer for the upscale model.

When it comes to the G.F.J., Zenith has acted like MacGyver, finding endless uses for its smash-hit model. First released in the spring of 2025, the watch received two very pretty, well-received sequels earlier this year. In March, I got to test out the upcoming onyx-dial version for just a few hours before I had to send it along to Hollywood stylist Fabio Immediato, who promptly strapped it on Simu Liu’s wrist for the Oscars.

Over the summer, Zenith also launched this double-signed program, which allows the brand to work with independent makers like J.N. Shapiro. Before this latest release, the Swiss brand linked up with Japan’s beloved Naoya Hida.

In a recent development, that watch was a fascinating representation of the project—the spotlessly clean dial was straight out of the latter’s workshop. Zenith, a historic brand backed by LVMH, ceded control entirely to the small Japanese indie. It was a massive success. To allocate the pieces, Marietta noted they narrowed the list to 10 clients, mainly from the Naoya Hida side, then sent an email that included the price tag of 60,000 Swiss francs but zero images of the watch. “They said yes right away, trusting us with the design,” Marietta said. “And that’s a great testimony of how the trust can be at that level when you buy a piece for [$75,000] without even seeing it, not even a picture.”.

According to recent reports, in the topsy-turvy world of watches in 2026, it’s much sexier to be an independent brand than one in the stable of the world’s largest luxury conglomerate. Marietta calls the G.F.J. “an independent brand within our global lineup,” pointing to the high-level finishing and historic movement inside the piece—the type of nerdy details that appeal to the most seasoned collectors driving the industry. “The G.F.J. collection itself is bringing us newly introduced clients,” Marietta said. “It's attracting clients who did not really have Zenith on their radar. These guys were more A. Lange & Söhne clients or with independents.”.

Zenith created irresistible bait for this new stripe of collectors. The new J.N. Shapiro-designed G.F.J. is absolutely gorgeous. The partners leverage the LA independent’s dedication to creating its dials by hand through a technique known as engine turning. I got to visit Shapiro’s workshop a few years ago and was charmed by the contrast of the brand’s cavernous industrial warehouse and the row of almost medieval-looking engine-turning machines lined up at the front of the room.

Recent findings suggest that the dials of the new collaborative watches were painstakingly made on those very machines—on which a single mistake means tossing the whole thing in the bin—and then shipped off to Switzerland, where Zenith watchmakers installed them into cases. There are three different patterns on the dial, including a basketweave at the center and Shapiro’s signature invention, the Infinity Weave, inside the subdial. Much like on the Naoya Hida version, the dial is all Shapiro. Marietta notes, however, that it already resembles the brick pattern seen on the original G.F.J., which is based on the exterior of Zenith’s manufacture in Le Locle.

According to recent reports, zenith plans to release two collaborative versions of the G.F.J. annually moving forward. According to Marietta, a couple of years down the road, the brand may allow their indie partners to go beyond the dial and play with the case and movement as well.

Sources indicate that with the G.F.J., Zenith has created something that is tailor-made for today’s collectors. Seven-figure pieces are at the moment booming at auction, and it would take Moses himself to part the money flooding into the market right now. These deep-pocketed collectors are most interested in watches from independent makers: Auction houses have sold more million-dollar F.P. Journe watches this year than they have from either Rolex or Patek Philippe. As collectors search for the next hot watchmaker, they’re finding exactly what they’re looking for in a 161-year-old Swiss luxury brand.

There isn’t just one way to experience Los Angeles, a place where glitz and glamour sit next to the natural beauty of California mountains and beaches, and the possibility of a movie star being around every corner brings a thrill to every day. As the iconic American designer Isaac Mizrahi once remarked, “I like to think glamour was invented in Hollywood,” and I tend to agree. There’s a thread of style in every aspect of life.

I recently headed to Los Angeles for ELLE’s Women in Hollywood event, one of our favorite nights of the year, and had a chance to revisit all this city has to offer. Our seminal Women in Hollywood issue honors the year’s most talented actresses, and each fall, in celebration of the issue, we host a star-studded party at the Four Seasons Los Angeles in Beverly Hills. For this month’s Insider Guide, I deliberated with true Angelenos, my friends Heidi Klum, interior designer Michael Smith, and fashion designer Sarah Staudinger, about the places they love the most in this classic West Coast destination.

Sources indicate that any time of year. Summer can be overly warm, and the perfect wintertime weather makes it an ideal getaway for East Coasters, but every season has something to offer. With LAX’s proximity to the city center, Los Angeles makes for an easy trip. I recommend renting a car to be able to visit all the beaches and experience the joy of driving down the Pacific Coast Highway, but Uber works just as well. Just be wary of the infamous Los Angeles traffic.

Industry News: How the ‘blue tsunami’ crested in North Carolina

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • LaKesha Womack faced towering odds as an underfunded Democrat making her first run for public office in a North Carolina district that Donald Trump carried by 15 points two years ago.
  • Industry observers note that but as early voting surged in mid-October, she sensed she might pull off an upset over Republican Rep.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

North Carolina Rep.-elect LaKesha Womack talks to reporters Sunday at the AC Hotel in Washington as she arrives for newly introduced member orientation. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

LaKesha Womack faced towering odds as an underfunded Democrat making her first run for public office in a North Carolina district that Donald Trump carried by 15 points two years ago.

Industry observers note that but as early voting surged in mid-October, she sensed she might pull off an upset over Republican Rep. Tim Moore, the influential former speaker of the North Carolina House and a chief architect of the gerrymander that aimed to keep the 14th District safely red.

According to recent reports, “There were a lot of pins and needles,” noted Womack, a 49-year-old ordained minister who works at a Charlotte-based nonprofit. After seeing long lines at polling places extend into Election Day, she grew more confident: “People were ready to exercise their voice.”.

Womack – who raised less than $60,000 to Moore’s $2.1 million – eked out a 2-point win in the district, which reaches from the Charlotte suburbs to mountain counties in the west.

Saddled with an unpopular president and broad dissatisfaction with the status quo, Republican incumbents across the nation experienced a midterm drubbing last week. As of Monday evening, House Democrats had netted 42 seats, with more races left to be called. The GOP in North Carolina, a state that Trump carried three times, was among the hardest hit.

According to recent reports, democrats have so far flipped five House seats in the Tar Heel State. Besides Womack, the “blue tsunami” also swept in Paul Barringer, a lawyer who founded an outdoor clothing line, and High Point Mayor Cyril Jefferson. And Army veteran Richard Ojeda, who once served in the West Virginia Senate, defeated Rep. Richard Hudson, the chairman of the National Republican Congressional Committee.

Recent findings suggest that democrats also won two races that had been seen as competitive for much of the cycle. Farmer Jamie Ager flipped an open seat in the state’s mountain west, while Rep. Don Davis held on to his Eastern North Carolina district, which Republicans had redrawn in their favor.

Meanwhile, in the state’s hilly northwest corner, 11-term Republican Virginia Foxx, the chairwoman of the powerful Rules Committee, is fighting for her political future: As of Monday afternoon, former journalist Chuck Hubbard led her by 99 votes in the 5th District, though The Associated Press had yet to call the race.

According to recent reports, that was also true in the neighboring 10th District, where GOP incumbent Pat Harrigan had a 1-point edge over Democratic physician associate Ashley Bell. Also uncalled were a pair of contests in Eastern North Carolina, where Republican Rep. Greg Murphy clung to a 233-vote edge over Democratic former state Rep. Raymond Smith and GOP Rep. David Rouzer led Democratic social worker Kimberly Hardy by less than a point.

“Nobody could have predicted this,’’ stated David Wilson Brown, who leads the Democratic Party in Gaston County near Charlotte and has lost two bids for the House, including to Foxx in 2020. “It’s a watershed moment.”.

The Democratic rout in the midterm elections was powered by victories in states with new GOP-favored maps, including Texas, Ohio and Florida.

But Democrats’ success in North Carolina was especially striking given the steep structural disadvantages the party faced. Since Republicans flipped the state legislature in 2010, and with it control of the redistricting process, no House GOP incumbent had lost a general election in the Tar Heel State until last week.

This year’s  congressional map – the state's sixth in seven election cycles – was engineered by the Republican-led legislature to help the party capture 11 of the state's 14 House seats.

Sources indicate that but the Democratic surge was so big that it easily overpowered the GOP’s built-in edge. Democratic candidates were also lifted by former Gov. Roy Cooper, whose 20-point Senate win provided the underticket with powerful coattails.

“In order for them to gerrymander our state in the way that they did, they were spread very thin,” Brown said, referring to state Republicans. “So they were kind of ripe to be defeated that way.”.

The repeated rounds of redistricting may have also erased some of the advantages of incumbency, according to Peter L. Francia, a political science professor at East Carolina University. “If you carve up a district every two years, you've taken away some of that [advantage]. And I think that that came back and hurt Republicans in this cycle.”.

Doug Heye, a GOP strategist and a former spokesman for the Republican National Committee, said redistricting “ticked off a whole lot of voters, and really activated the Democratic base.”.

On the Republican side, voters were “less motivated because they were unexcited about Trump,’’ Heye added.

Republican incumbents accustomed to winning by comfortable margins weren’t prepared for a political environment driven by anger over the war in Iran and angst about the rising cost of living.

Recent findings suggest that “Clearly, a lot of those Republicans didn’t take their elections seriously,” Heye stated. “They won last time with 18 points. They weren't on anyone's radar screen, so they didn't think they had to do anything.”.

Womack credits her win to a grassroots campaign centered on economic challenges. While her race wasn’t on the national radar – Moore, after all, won by 16 points in 2024 – and her campaign didn’t have money for ads, she was out in the district doing events every day.

“There are a lot of working families right now who are in the missing middle,” she said in an interview. “They make too much money to get help, but they don't make enough money to get ahead. … Someone who can be working a full-time job, but still doesn’t have enough money to buy groceries or to afford their medications or to have access to health insurance.”.

Womack mentioned her own struggles have shaped her approach to politics. This week, she’s slated to appear in court on a felony charge for allegedly failing to return a rental car in 2019. The incident wound up in one of Moore’s attack ads.

Industry observers note that “There are so many people who [understand] what happens when you're down on your luck and you don't have enough money to make good financial decisions,’’ she noted. “Most people don't want those bad decisions to be a definition of their character for the rest of their life.”.

Early in the midterm cycle, Democratic opposition research group American Bridge prepared detailed dossiers on Republican House incumbents in North Carolina.

“Someone like Virginia Foxx, she’s been on the Hill forever,” stated Pat Dennis, the group’s president. “She was somebody … who under the radar could be vulnerable. So we started really early.”.

American Bridge’s political arm spent $340,000 on ads targeting Foxx. One spot featured a man who identified himself as a Trump voter expressing anger at the government’s response to Hurricane Helene, which devastated the mountain communities of Western North Carolina two years ago.

Other Democrats scoffed at the group’s decision to spend money targeting entrenched Republicans far from the main House battleground.

“There was a lot of reluctance from people to really believe that that data was correct, but it was,’’ Dennis said. “Then over the summer, we saw her numbers collapsing, so we put paid media behind it and it really paid off.”.

Hubbard ran against Foxx two years ago and lost by almost 20 points.

“I kind of had a notion I was going to do this again,’’ he said in an interview Saturday while en route to Washington for freshman orientation. “I don’t like to lose at checkers, much less a congressional race.”.

After a court-drawn map resulted in a split North Carolina delegation after the 2022 elections, state Republicans won back control of the map-making process and went on to win 10 of the state’s 14 House seats under a latest map two years later.

At Trump’s urging, Republicans made further tweaks to the North Carolina map last year, but the original gerrymander finally came back to bite the GOP in 2026, according to Hubbard.

“North Carolina is one of the most severely gerrymandered states,’’ he stated. “And what happened was they had to steal from Peter to pay Paul. It's been referred to by political scientists as a dummymander.”.

As the vote count in the 5th District continues, Foxx, whose campaign declined to comment for this story, has requested the presence of nonpartisan election observers.

They “will serve as key, watchful eyes to ensure that this sacred process is not impeded and that all legal votes are counted in a consistent, thorough manner,’’ she posted on social media.

But even before the final races are called, Republicans are already looking to the next election.

In a recent development, heye, who expects North Carolina to remain a purple state in 2028 and beyond, cautioned the Democrats who won last week not to get too comfortable in Washington. He invoked Fred Heineman, the former Raleigh police chief who rode the 1994 “Republican Revolution” to Congress – and lasted a single term.

“Some of them will lose, and some of the people who lost may run two years from now and get their seat back,’’ he remarked.

One GOP operative, who requested anonymity to speak candidly, offered up a similar assessment.

Trump “didn't keep his promises” and that “just got voters very angry and suppressed the GOP base from coming out because, in a midterm election it's a base turnout contest,’’ the strategist said.

“But these Democrats are renting these districts for two years.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The recent buzz around peptides came to a head last month when U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) Robert F. Kennedy Jr. announced that six unregulated injectables, including the highly controversial “Wolverine stack” BPC-157 and TB-500, will now be available for broad use throughout the United States. Meanwhile, unsurprising to derms and estheticians everywhere, the rising tide of interest in peptides has spilled over into skincare, where the molecules have long served as an active ingredient.

“I’ve had a lot of patients come in since the HHS ruling,” states Erik Peterson, MD, a board-certified dermatologist in New York City, who likens the recent policy change to “opening the floodgates,” resulting in a surge of interest—particularly from patients who’ve come across claims of peptide-based skincare being like ‘botox in a bottle.’.

Sources indicate that “It’s interesting how they are suddenly so popular, because peptides have been around for like 30 years in skincare,” says Malika Sloan, medical esthetician and founder of Sloan Studio in New York City. “They’ve been incorporated into cosmetic formulations for decades, with ingredients like matrixyl helping to popularize them in the early 2000s. What’s exciting now is how much more sophisticated the formulations have become.”.

If you’re curious about peptide-based skincare products—what they potentially can do, what they definitely cannot—and which products experts recommend for the best results, here’s everything you need to know.

Industry observers note that peptides, regardless of whether they’re injected via syringe or applied topically with a serum or cream, are short chains of amino acids that instruct your body to execute specific functions. Insulin, for example, is a peptide that helps the body regulate blood sugar, and it’s been in use since the 1920s. More recently, GLP-1 drugs (short for glucagon-like peptide-1) have been found to curb food cravings and slow stomach emptying, making them highly effective for weight loss. The list of uses for peptides is virtually endless, ranging from muscle growth and wound healing to balancing hormones and managing inflammation.

In skincare, topical peptides work much the same way as their injectable counterparts, but on a more localized level, directing your skin to carry out specific functions, “the first of which tends to be increasing production of collagen and elastin, which are two of the major determinants of skin quality,” indicates Dr. Peterson. They’ve also been shown to help even out skin tone, repair the skin barrier, and reduce the appearance of fine lines and wrinkles.

The world of peptides is still a bit of a Wild West. A quick Google search for peptide skincare will yield dozens of results for unresearched compounds promising you flawless skin. And then, of course, there are the influencers. “You see all these kids on TikTok who are talking about their beauty routines, and they’re like 19 years old,” indicates Peterson. “It’s like, ‘Amazing, your skin obviously looks great, because you’re a child.’” In reality, the list of peptides that you can truly depend on to move the needle (without an actual needle) is surprisingly short, at least until more research is done.

In a recent development, “The two peptides that are out right now that have any sort of viable data on them are palmitoyl pentapeptide-4 and GHK-Cu,” claims Peterson. Signaling peptides, as they’re called—such as palmitoyl pentapeptide-4, better known as matrixyl—have some of the strongest clinical and anecdotal evidence for stimulating collagen and reducing the appearance of wrinkles. Although, as Peterson points out, much of the scientific data has been industry funded, “so we always have to be a bit skeptical.”.

Sources indicate that carrier peptides—like GHK-Cu, a popular copper peptide—on the other hand, “have some good lab data, but very minimal human data,” Peterson says. Nonetheless, products containing GHK-Cu are widely heralded for their ability to repair damaged tissue, reduce inflammation, and stimulate production of collagen and elastin. “I find copper peptides particularly interesting because of the research surrounding tissue repair and collagen-related remodeling pathways,” says Sloan.

It has been revealed that as for acetyl hexapeptide-8, or argireline, as it’s more commonly known—aka “botox in a bottle”—don’t waste your money. “From a physiological perspective, it can’t possibly work,” states Peterson, who explains that the molecules of this particular peptide are simply too large to pass through the surface of the skin. He compares it to skincare products that contain collagen rather than spur the body to produce its own. “Collagen is a massive molecule,” he says. “It would be like putting cow’s milk on your face—it’s not going to do anything.” Sure enough, a 2023 study found the effects of topical argireline to be “not statistically significant.”.

Instead, for those looking for the most noticeable results, Sloan recommends seeking out products that combine proven peptides with complementary, similarly validated ingredients—like SkinCeuticals’ P-TIOX Anti-Wrinkle Peptide Cream. “I like that the cream also incorporates ceramides, niacinamide, and moisturizing ingredients, making it an interesting option for someone looking to address both hydration and visible signs of aging,” she claims. Peterson’s pick, The Rich Cream from Augustinus Bader, flanks signaling peptides with hyaluronic acid and vitamin E to improve moisture retention and bolster the skin’s protective barrier.

Peptides are a relatively low-maintenance addition to most skin regimens. “One of the reasons I love incorporating peptides into at-home skincare is that they’re generally well tolerated and relatively easy to combine with other ingredients,” indicates Sloan, who notes that peptides can typically be used alongside other popular actives like vitamin C, niacinamide, hyaluronic acid, and retinoids. “I typically recommend incorporating a peptide serum after cleansing and before moisturizer,” she says.

Just keep in mind that peptides alone won’t take the place of a well-rounded skincare regimen. “The best, most robust data still comes from the tried-and-true favorites of all dermatologists—protecting your collagen with consistent sunscreen use, and the best signaling molecule of them all: topical retinoids,” Peterson indicates.

According to recent reports, and, of course, don’t expect overnight results—despite what social media might have you believe. “Peptides are just signals for your skin, not magic in a bottle,” Peterson says. “The few studies that there are show at least three months of consistent usage before results are seen, so stick it out if you want to give it a real try.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We rate butternut the most affable winter squash—relatively easy to prepare, consistently delicious, and available at most grocery stores. The buttered nut dressing is more than just cheeky wordplay. Bold from brown butter and balsamic vinegar and bright from lemon, the crunchy topping is an excellent foil to the sweetness of roasted squash. Cook the squash a couple hours ahead of time and all you’ll have left to do before dinner is make the dressing.

For more Thanksgiving recipes, tips, menus, and inspiration, head to our 2026 Thanksgiving Hub.

It has been revealed that place a rack in lower third of oven; preheat to 425°. Lightly crush 2 tsp. fennel seeds with a mortar and pestle or place on a cutting board and gently crush with a heavy pan. Peel 1 medium butternut squash (about 3 lb.) and halve lengthwise. Scoop out seeds; discard. Cut squash into 2" irregular pieces, aiming for sharp, jagged shapes. Transfer to a large rimmed baking sheet; drizzle with 3 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil and sprinkle with fennel seeds, 2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and 1 tsp. crushed red pepper flakes. Toss squash to coat, arrange in a single layer, and roast until browned and tender, 30–35 minutes.

Do Ahead: Squash can be roasted 2 hours ahead. Store at room temperature.

According to recent reports, while the squash is roasting, cook 6 oz. thick-cut bacon, cut into 1" pieces, in a medium skillet over medium heat, stirring often, until browned and mostly crisp, 8–12 minutes. Transfer to a small plate with a slotted spoon.

According to recent reports, reduce heat to low; combine 1 cup raw pecans and 4 Tbsp. unsalted butter in same pan. Cook, stirring often, until butter browns and nuts have slightly darkened, 6–8 minutes. Remove from heat. Stir in 3 garlic cloves, finely chopped (this will give it a head start to take off the raw edge), then add bacon, zest and juice of 1 large lemon, 3 sprigs sage, and 2 Tbsp. balsamic vinegar and stir to combine. Taste dressing and season with kosher salt if needed.

Arrange squash on a platter and spoon dressing over.

Cecilie Bahnsen has a cult following for a reason: the Danish designer’s big blooming dresses and dedication to sporty, easy balletcore have been collected in droves by fashion far and wide. So when Uniqlo came calling for her to design a second collaboration, it was time again for the designer to take the reins and merge her playful girlish Scandi style with the utilitarian wearability of the Japanese giant. The collection, which includes womenswear and childrenswear, puts a focus on cozy winter wardrobe dressing and is available now. In it, Bahnsen is rethinking and retooling the classic winter fleece.

Sources indicate that for the occasion, Bahnsen spent half a year designing the collection and also collaborated with her friend Fumiko Imano, the artist, to shoot the campaign in Sweden amidst a picturesque landscape. “It was very much about sisterhood, the journey you do of exploring together, and inspiration also from when I’m in the countryside with my son, and we collect flowers, and how we kind of, he sometimes pinned them on his jumper,” Bahnsen tells ELLE of the upcoming collection. “I think it was really kind of that romantic or nostalgic feeling that I wanted to put into the collection. And then there was also this notion of just working with one fabrication and working with the fleece for winter and how you can work this as layering.”.

While Bahnsen in particular is known for her flouncy babydoll dresses, when it came to her second collection for Uniqlo, she tells us it was all about “refinement and balance and creating beautiful kind of everyday pieces.” Her personal favorite piece of the lineup is the fleece in the palest shade of soft pastel pink, embroidered with small flowers. “For me, the fleece is such a classic layering piece,” she says. She’s already been wearing it herself for countryside outings. “There’s romance and nostalgia to pink, and I think with this collaboration, it was nice to do the fleece in pink,” she says. “Showing that it could have that femininity to it was special, and it is also that right tone as a super soft pink that I love.”.

In a recent development, the entire collection is designed to be layered, and the fleece is at the center of it. There’s a cropped fleece vest, a sheer long T-shirt printed with subtle bouquets of flowers, a floral-embellished fleece skirt and matching socks, gloves, and hats. Bahnsen herself recommends taking a cue from her own runway reveals. “I always love a big jumper or a big fleece over a poof-y dress,” she claims. “It has both a super boyish vibe to it but also a princess-y, romantic feeling, too, so I love those kinds of contrasts between each other.”.

In a recent development, “These are pieces that you want to not just to work for one season, but to be timeless; it’s become about the perfection of these small details that makes it unique and maybe more romantic than what is normally in the Uniqlo collection,” adds Bahnsen. “I feel like the palette has a really Scandinavian winter tone to it, so how do you balance this soft pink into the darker blacks and blues, and kind of build it up, not in a monocomatic way, but really putting the tones and the layering together.” It’s definitely a chicer way to stay warm. The designer’s latest is the ultimate study of form and function.

Few literary presses can claim a Rolodex as studded with boldface names as Farrar, Straus and Giroux. This week, the publishing house, whose authors have been awarded dozens of National Book Awards, Pulitzer Prizes, and Nobel Prizes in Literature, toasted its 80th anniversary with a distinguished fête in Manhattan’s Chelsea neighborhood.

The guest list, which gathered prominent cultural and artistic personages, featured a mix of FSG’s coterie of best-selling writers from over the years. The night united early-career contemporary authors like Madeline Cash (Lost Lambs) and Raven Leilani (Luster) with established literary lions such as Jonathan Franzen, André Aciman, and Jeffrey Eugenides. The decorated crowd also included filmmaker John Waters, Emmy Award winner Rebecca Miller, actor and editor Tavi Gevinson, and booksellers James Daunt and Sarah McNally.

Sources indicate that the evening was hosted by president and publisher Mitzi Angel, who became the first woman to lead the house when she stepped into her position in 2022. Before and during her tenure at FSG Angel worked with authors including Sheila Heti, Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie, Rachel Cusk, Garth Greenwell, and Sally Rooney. Though cognizant of the role of algorithms in the economy of taste, Angel expressed “great faith” in the current and future state of publishing and the literary arts. “I feel more certain than ever that good writing can arrive in our hands at any moment, from anywhere,” Angel told Vogue, surveying the mingling throng of writers she’d published. “I think all of us here in this room understand that it only takes one person to reframe reality altogether: one person, a writer.”.

Sources indicate that guests were treated to a soaring performance of Philip Glass’s “Songs from Liquid Days” by Anthony Roth Costanzo (whose debut memoir Countertenor was published last month), fresh off his starring turn in Lincoln in the Bardo at the Met. The revelry continued into the night with sounds from Fresh York City funk and soul band The Ruckus and a late-night surprise DJ set by multiple-Grammy-winning artist Ahmir Thompson, better known as Questlove, who also just so happens to be the publisher of FSG imprint AUWA Books.

And what, according to Angel, is the common denominator among the stable of scribes? “FSG writers have something key to say—and they know how to say it,” she mentioned. “For them, the special alchemy between language and what it describes is crucial.”.

Why You Should Never Put Frozen Meat In A Slow Cooker, According To Experts

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (787 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Delish

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that with busy schedules and limited time each day, slow cookers are key to getting dinner on the table.
  • The idea seems convenient in theory, but in practice, it raises some serious food safety concerns.
  • Sorry to be the bearer of bad news: You should never put frozen meat directly into your slow cooker.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that with busy schedules and limited time each day, slow cookers are key to getting dinner on the table. They can take simple ingredients and transform them into a complete, ready-to-eat meal. Because the slow cooker does all the work for you, you may think that it can also handle defrosting meat.

But think again. The idea seems convenient in theory, but in practice, it raises some serious food safety concerns. We consulted health experts to learn more about adding frozen meat to a slow cooker. So next time you plan a hands-off dinner, you can make sure your food is delicious and safe to eat.

Sorry to be the bearer of bad news: You should never put frozen meat directly into your slow cooker. “I am all for cutting out unnecessary steps in cooking, but using frozen meat in your slow cooker is not one of them,” claims Melissa Koch, RD, MEd.

Recent findings suggest that raw meat can carry harmful bacteria that cause foodborne illness. Freezing stops them from multiplying, but doesn't necessarily kill them. And because slow cookers heat food gradually, frozen meat can spend too long in what food safety experts call the “temperature danger zone.”.

In a recent development, “The danger zone refers to a temperature range of 40°F (4°C) to 140°F (60°C) over two or more hours when harmful bacteria grow or multiply at a fast rate,” Koch explains. It can take hours for food in a slow cooker to move above the danger zone—and starting with frozen meat delays that process even further.

Sources indicate that “The appliance heats food slowly, and starting with frozen meat means the internal temperature may sit in the ‘danger zone’ for too long,” claims chef and dietitian Sharniquia White. “This gives bacteria like Salmonella or E. coli more opportunity to multiply before the food reaches a safe cooking temperature.”.

Recent findings suggest that what happens after eating food that has sat in the danger zone? The consequences vary based on your immune system, the extent of the contamination, and the strains of bacteria present. But none are pleasant, and some may even send you to the hospital.

Sources indicate that “Symptoms of food-borne illness can include nausea, vomiting, stomach cramps, and fever,” Koch indicates. “You can experience the effects of food-borne illness within a few minutes to days after consuming a load of harmful pathogens or bacteria.”.

According to recent reports, cooking frozen meat on the “low” setting of your slow cooker increases the time it spends in the danger zone, but the risk is present regardless. “The 'high' setting reduces the amount of time food spends at unsafe temperatures, but still doesn’t fully eliminate the risk when starting with frozen meat,” indicates White.

In a recent development, the ingredients you're using can also increase your risk. “Larger, denser cuts (like roasts or whole poultry) take longer to thaw and heat evenly, so they pose a greater risk of staying at unsafe temperatures for extended periods,” White explains.

In a recent development, smaller pieces may thaw faster, but that doesn't necessarily make them safe to cook from frozen. White explains that ground meat is “particularly risky” because of the way it's processed, so it should be cooked thoroughly.

“I feed three young children at my home, so in my opinion, I wouldn't chance cooking frozen meat, no matter the size, in a slow cooker,” Koch states.

It has been revealed that the answer is simple: thaw your meat before turning on your slow cooker. But your ideal method depends on how much time you have.

The safest, easiest, and least involved thawing method is to put your frozen meat in the fridge. The cold temperature of your refrigerator lets your food defrost gently without entering the danger zone.

Our editors recommend placing the meat on a plate or baking sheet to collect any juices and avoid contaminating other food in your fridge. This process can take anywhere from a couple of hours to a couple of days, depending on the cut of meat. “This requires some thought and effort, but in the long run it's worth your safety,” Koch says.

In a recent development, no time for that? No problem. You can thaw meat faster by submerging it in cold water in a leakproof bag, changing the water every 30 minutes, or defrosting it in the microwave, though the latter can compromise the meat's texture. Both methods require cooking the meat immediately afterward. “Once thawed, meat should go directly into the slow cooker,” White explains.

It all takes a little extra effort and planning, but it's worth it to avoid getting sick from your slow cooker dinner.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, in the 1980s, Azzedine Alaïa acquired a title that followed him for the rest of his career: the “King of Cling.” The moniker was a fitting one: the Tunisian couturier was renowned for his sculptural, body-centric designs. He experimented with stretch jersey and “anti-stress” fibers to sculpt the body without restricting movement.

According to recent reports, but the nickname was also limiting, failing to capture the full scope of his work. The first major U.S. retrospective devoted to Alaïa, “Azzedine Alaïa: Sculpting Fashion,” at San Francisco’s Legion of Honor, brings his broader legacy into focus through 80 garments and selections from his personal collection of historic fashion.

“As my research went on, I came to realize how important the U.S. market was in Alaïa’s launch,” Laura L. Camerlengo, co-curator of the exhibit and curator in charge of Costume and Textile Arts at the Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco, tells ELLE. “By the [brand’s] third season, the U.S. was the second highest market after France, [with interest from] both luxury department stores and small independent retailers.”.

According to recent reports, the exhibition took shape after Camerlengo reached out to Olivier Saillard, director of the Fondation Azzedine Alaïa in Paris, who became her co-curator. As visitors enter the Legion of Honor’s Rosekrans Court, they encounter a dress designed for Grace Jones: a spring/summer 1986 haute couture look that Jones modeled on the runway and wore to the 1985 Oscars de la Mode. Part of the opening display, titled “The Women Who Made Alaïa,” it sets the tone for a show that recognizes the muses—both famous and private clients—who wore and supported his work.

Also on view are looks made famous by Rihanna—namely, a sheer red halter gown with a flowing train that she wore to the 2013 Grammys—and Tina Turner, whose silk-organza dress embroidered with gold-tone beads from Alaïa’s spring/summer 1989 concludes the exhibition.

Industry observers note that the show then turns to Alaïa’s iconography, as Camerlengo puts it: the bandage dress, his work in denim, and zippered dresses, as well as rare, lesser-seen gems. “I was really keen to have early works on view, particularly the pieces from the 1980s, when he was launching his brand,” the curator says. “These are pieces that would have been shown at Bergdorf Goodman when he had his first fashion show in the United States.”.

The exhibition also places Alaïa’s designs in conversation with the museum’s permanent collection. Belle Epoque-style ensembles from his spring/summer 1992 collection appear among 18th-century European paintings and furnishings, including a Canaletto view of Venice and a sofa commissioned for Marie Antoinette.

Industry observers note that alaïa’s own collection of historic fashion, previously shown in the 2023 Paris exhibition “Azzedine Alaïa, couturier collectionneur,” is represented here, too. The gallery includes pieces by fashion houses he admired, such as Lanvin, Chanel, Balenciaga, and Schiaparelli.

Recent findings suggest that though Alaïa, who died in 2017 at age 82, is remembered for the body-conscious designs that earned him that “King of Cling” title, he was also a renegade in an industry built around constant production. He showed collections only when he felt they were ready—a maverick approach that still resonates today—and had his creations worn by a who’s who of the modeling world, from Naomi Campbell to Gisele Bündchen. Many of his designs were featured in the pages of ELLE over the decades.

Industry observers note that “He was someone who pioneered a new way of thinking about fashion,” Camerlengo claims. “He was one of the first to question the fashion system and seasonal calendars and the need for trends. He was focused on meticulous craftsmanship and intentionality in design, a sort of precedent to what we think about today, where we are critical of overproduction and overconsumption in fashion.”.

“Azzedine Alaïa: Sculpting Fashion” is on view at the Legion of Honor Museum from Nov. 21, 2026, to Apr. 11, 2027.

Shohei Ohtani is used to making history. In addition to his four MLB MVP awards and two World Series rings, the Los Angeles Dodgers two-way great is the first member of the 50/50 club (having racked up 54 home runs and 59 stolen bases during the 2024 season), became the first player to hit three homers and record 10 strikeouts in a single game (which he managed in a 2025 NLCS contest against the Brewers), and earlier this year maintained simultaneous streaks in games on base (48) and innings without an earned run (32 and two-thirds).

In a recent development, now, the 32-year-old Japanese icon is adding to those accolades with a pioneering endorsement deal, officially extending his relationship with his longtime partner Fresh Balance through to the end of his baseball career. (While a rarefied group of athletes have signed lifetime sponsorship deals—including LeBron James and Cristiano Ronaldo at Nike, and Damian Lillard at Adidas—Ohtani’s new contract appears to be both the first to exclusively cover a star’s playing days and the first of its kind in MLB.).

Sources indicate that “There’s a lot of trust,” Ohtani tells me through an interpreter during a sit-down in Boston of his decision to commit to the New England sportswear stalwart for the long haul. “We’ve obviously built friendships, as well. They’ve been able to accommodate my requests, the things I’ve asked for, and, like I said, that takes the involvement of a lot of trust. That relationship has been very, very good and smooth. I had no reservations about extending our relationship.”.

Sources indicate that earlier in the day, I shadowed Ohtani at Fresh Balance’s headquarters, where, as part of the agreement, the manufacturer is renaming its on-site think tank as the Shohei Ohtani Sports Research Lab. A team of specialists led the Dodgers superstar through a slew of shoes—including his on-field Ohtani 1 model, which will receive new editions in 2027—and then a rack of branded apparel. All of it falls under his Shohei Ohtani Signature Collection, which New Balance introduced in 2024 (about a year and a half after the athlete first signed with the company). The collection has grown deliberately and unhurriedly ever since—mirroring his patience in the batter’s box; Ohtani is methodical when it comes to product development and uninterested in rolling out rushed goods with his name slapped on them.

While conducting a kind of footwear postmortem on his 2026 season—which started well, but ended with a rare slump (and left knee and right biceps injuries that kept him from pitching after July 3)—Ohtani noted there’d been some moments of slippage on the heel of his landing foot when pitching. On a printed-out diagram, he used a pencil to sketch ways in which the shoe’s spikes might be slightly reconfigured to find a sweet spot for stability on the mound and speed around the bases. The question of switching footwear between pitching and batting comes up, but Ohtani has not yet done this (and it seems the consensus is to stick with one shoe only).

Industry observers note that “I have a lot of direct input into the footwear and apparel,” Ohtani notes. “That includes my style, which I like to keep simple, as well as performance-based requests, [like with my] spikes. Some years we make minor changes, and sometimes we’ll make a significant change. They understand what I want.”.

According to recent reports, ohtani’s apparel line runs across three categories: performance, lifestyle, and fanwear. His custom logo—a striking ink drawing of his figure, designed by the Japanese manga artist Takehiko Inoue—is featured subtly on the bulk of the lineup. “Shohei doesn’t see himself as a glamorous player,” Chris Davis, New Balance brand president and chief marketing officer, tells me. “He sees himself as a gritty, hardworking athlete who wants to get better every day, and his logo reflects this—it has this kind of quiet intensity.”.

In a recent development, while some of the future apparel designs boast cool technical features—like detachable, two-in-one, and reversible elements inspired by Ohtani’s two-way play—the man himself is only concerned that his products “fit comfortably and to be easy to wear.” When asked if there’s anyone whose style he likes or is influenced by, Ohtani shrugs. “Honestly, not really. I just like to wear what I like to wear.”.

It has been revealed that “[Shohei] is very quick and clear with his input,” indicates Masahiro Uchida, New Balance’s general manager of athlete signature product, who has worked alongside Ohtani for years. “On the performance side, he always prefers softness and a soft hand feel. For the lifestyle side, he prefers clean and simple. He also understands the occasion. He always asks us, ‘Where would I wear this?’” One major goal for Ohtani with his apparel, Uchida adds, is to “support the expansion of baseball culture and show his respect for its heritage. He is a super geek about MLB. He knows so much.”.

Industry observers note that at 32, the duration of Ohtani’s career—and, now, his Upcoming Balance deal—remains an open question. That age can be considered as getting toward the older end in pro baseball, but elite pitchers have a habit of playing well into their 40s—Justin Verlander, for example, just pitched his final season at 43.

Industry observers note that ohtani still intends on being a full two-way player in 2027, with hopes for a Cy Young Award—MLB’s top pitching honor, one of the few laurels he has yet to win—still alive. When the Dodgers’ season ended on October 15, Ohtani told the press that he was “not quite satisfied with how things shaped up on the pitching side.”.

What words of advice or motivation does he have, I ask, for the legion of kids hoping to follow in his footsteps? His answer feels like something he might be saying to himself as the next season approaches.

It has been revealed that “If you want to become successful, baseball is a sport that takes a lot of repetitive practice,” he states. “You always have to work on your fundamentals. Once you reach a certain level, the sport becomes very, very hard. At that point, you need to remember why you’re playing. Are you playing because you love the sport? If you have that drive, that love for it, then even when it’s tough, you can overcome it.”.

For those who might shudder at the thought of eating raw hardy greens like collards or kale, this vibrant side inspired by the French bistro classic leeks vinaigrette is the answer. Simmered past squeaky-raw yet well short of meltingly braised, they offer substantial bite, like al dente pasta. The mustard dressing couldn’t be simpler to make—use it as a base for any salad you might serve this season. It’s punchy enough to stand up to winter vegetables or any sturdy bitter green.

For more Thanksgiving recipes, tips, menus, and inspiration, head to our 2026 Thanksgiving Hub.

It has been revealed that place a rack in middle of oven; preheat to 325°. Toast ½ cup raw walnuts on a rimmed baking sheet, tossing halfway through, until golden brown, 10–12 minutes.

Meanwhile, cook 2 bunches collard greens, ribs and stems removed, leaves cut into 2" pieces, in a large pot of generously salted boiling water until just tender, 9–11 minutes. Using tongs, immediately transfer to a large bowl of ice water and let cool.

Whisk 2 garlic cloves, finely grated, ¼ cup white wine vinegar, 2 Tbsp. Dijon mustard, preferably country-style, ⅓ cup extra-virgin olive oil, ¼ cup (packed) coarsely chopped tarragon, 2 tsp. sugar, and 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt in a medium bowl to combine. Set dressing aside.

Sources indicate that transfer toasted walnuts to a small bowl and drizzle with remaining 1 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil. Sprinkle with a generous pinch each of sugar and salt and toss to coat. Taste and add more sugar if needed (nuts should be more sweet than salty). Set seasoned walnuts aside.

Drain collard greens and squeeze gently to remove excess water. Transfer to bowl with reserved dressing and toss to coat evenly. Cover and chill at least 15 minutes and up to 2 hours.

According to recent reports, arrange greens in a shallow bowl or on a platter and spoon any dressing remaining in bowl over. Top with seasoned walnuts and tarragon leaves.

Sources indicate that do Ahead: Walnuts can be toasted and dressing can be made 1 day ahead. Store walnuts airtight at room temperature. Cover dressing and chill.

According to recent reports, we Are All Human, through its Hispanic Star initiative, is a nonprofit aimed at uplifting Hispanics in economic and cultural spaces. According to its website, “Hispanic Star seeks to reframe Hispanics not merely as a fast-growing demographic, but as a vital economic, cultural, and civic force shaping the United States’ future.”.

In a recent development, throughout the evening, many leaders were recognized for their contributions to society. These included fashion designer Willy Chavarria, CEO and creative director of Willy Chavarria; Mark D. Levine, Fresh York City comptroller; Bea Perez, executive vice president and global chief communications, sustainability, and strategic partnerships officer at The Coca-Cola Organization, and chair of The Coca-Cola Foundation; and Henry R. Muñoz III, American activist and founder and CEO of Cultural Productions.

According to recent reports, “For generations, our people have been told where we can go, how far we can rise, and which doors we’re allowed to walk through on our own land,” Chavarria noted in his speech. “Now, it’s the time for us to change all of that. When one of us succeeds, we all get a little bit more powerful.”.

In a recent development, other individuals were also inducted into the organization’s CMO Hall of Fame, and various community organizers and tastemakers gave testimonials on We Are All Human’s impact in their lives. The late labor leader Dolores Huerta was also honored in a moving tribute, and Chavarria also mentioned the feminist activist in his speech. “She carried such strength and humanity and grace, and we all learned from her,” the designer stated. “In this time when we see our brothers and sisters and our brown friends and family being treated like animals and abducted and sent away and put in camps and all of that, it’s just so notable for us to stand tall in who we are right now.”.

Cirque du Soleil took the stage to perform, and guests were given shots of Sotol Romo in champagne flutes for a toast. Co-chairs Gabriel de Alba, founder and managing partner of GDA Luma Capital Management; Karla Martínez de Salas, chief content officer of AVANCE; Bing Chen, CEO and co-founder of Gold House; and Marissa Solis, SVP of global brand and consumer marketing of the NFL, also attended the event. We Are All Human also surpassed its fundraising goals, with two individuals spending $32,000 on a Super Bowl package during the live auction.

“The We Are All Human Foundation is equipped to turn this momentum into results, through data and insights, to guide decisions and to inspire others,” Romo Edelman told the crowd. “Our co-chairs and honorees are the pure embodiment of the Latino brand that we want the world to see.”.

In a recent development, after a 13-year drought, Grand Theft Auto VI has finally hit the masses. Predictably, a large swath of guys have called off work to give themselves just enough time to explore the immersive fictional land of Leonida, where players can do just about everything they can in real life—from driving cars and renovating homes to playing video games within a video game. In Grand Theft Auto VI, that now also includes hitting the gym. And if you want to progress through the story as efficiently as possible, becoming an in-game gym rat might be the best thing you can do.

Expanding on a gameplay mechanic introduced in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, working out in GTA levels up your character to help with progressing through the story. The fitter you become in the game, the more stamina you have to sprint, the more health you have before you’re Wasted, and the more focus you have to take down enemies. Just like in real life, pumping iron makes daily life a whole lot easier.

Recent findings suggest that to get fit, you can use the weights in Jason’s outdoor gym, which features the massive three full-body lifts: squats, bench presses, and deadlifts. While your character handles the heavy lifting, all you have to do is carefully time your button presses to complete reps without causing an injury. Once you have enough money, you can purchase memberships at gyms across the city, giving you access to treadmills, free weights, and workout machines. The exercise options are so extensive (you can even do zone 2 cardio) that gamers have already started trading tips to the best GTA 6 workouts for maximizing your character’s gains.

Recent findings suggest that as your character gets stronger, their avatar transforms accordingly, developing more defined muscles, a six-pack, and even a chiseled face. Neglecting your fitness and overeating (a real thing you can do in the game) has an alternate effect as your player visibly gains weight and adopts a “dad bod.”.

Industry observers note that inevitably there will be many players that skip the gym this weekend so they can pump a little virtual iron with their thumbs. There’s something undeniably ironic about looksmaxxing your GTA character while spending hours sitting on the couch playing a video game. But don’t think that just because it’s all on a screen that you won’t walk away from a session with a little back pain, so maybe schedule a few breaks in between. You could even build a home gym of your own like Jason’s—it’s already got one fitness expert’s approval.

In a large bowl, beat egg whites with a large pinch of salt on medium-high speed with a handheld mixer (or in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the whisk attachment) until foamy, which should take about one minute.

While beating, slowly add sugar and beat until meringue is thick and glossy, which should take about 7 minutes. Beat in vinegar, cornstarch, and vanilla until well combined.

According to recent reports, pile the meringue in the center of a parchment-lined baking sheet. Using a spatula or spoon, spread the mixture into an 8" circle. Make a small well in the center.

According to recent reports, transfer to the oven, and immediately reduce the oven temperature to 250°. Bake the meringue until set but still white, which should take about an hour. Turn off the oven and let the pavlova cool completely in the oven for at least 2 hours and up to overnight. Transfer cooled pavlova to a platter.

Top with whipped cream and berries.

The full list of ingredients and instructions can be found in the recipe below.

Store the unassembled pavlova in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days, keeping it away from humidity. Once topped with whipped cream and fresh fruit, refrigerate and enjoy within a day, as the meringue will soften over time.
